# `js/skipped-test`

**A skipped test has a reason and an expiry**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/markers` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (why a test is off, and until when, is a fact only the author knows; the engine can't write it) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |

## What it checks

A test turned off with `.skip` (`it.skip`, `test.skip`, `describe.skip`, `test.describe.skip`, `it.skip.each(…)`) or with Jasmine's and Mocha's `xit`, `xdescribe`, `xtest`, `xcontext`, `xspecify` says why and until when. Playwright's `test.skip(condition, "reason")` already carries its reason in the call; the expiry still goes in a `SKIP` comment.

The reason comes from the framework's own argument where it has one, else from the text of a **`SKIP` comment** on the line directly above the test (or at the end of its first line): `// SKIP(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): reason`. The ticket and the date are in the parentheses, in either order. The expiry is the date the skip stops being allowed: it is **expired** from the as-of date on (`--as-of`, `CODELAW_AS_OF`, else `HEAD`'s commit date, never the clock: [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md) decision 9) and is a **warning** for the `warn_days` before it. A skip whose `SKIP` comment names a date that has come is an error at the skipped test.

**Why:** A skipped test is a check that is switched off, and nothing shows it. A reason says why, an expiry makes it come back for review on a day somebody agreed to, and a failing skip on that day is how it gets turned on again instead of staying off for years.

**Configuration** is the `[tests.skip]` table of `codelaw.toml` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md) decision 11a), shared by `js/skipped-test` and `py/skipped-test`:

```toml
[tests.skip]
require_reason = true    # a reason is required (default)
require_expiry = true    # a SKIP(…, date) expiry is required (default)
require_ticket = false   # a ticket is required (default: no)
ticket_pattern = "[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\\d+"
warn_days      = 14      # warn this many days before the expiry
```

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/markers` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/markers"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/skipped-test" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/skipped-test" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/skipped-test" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/skipped-test" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/skipped-test" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/skipped-test": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/skipped-test: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/skipped-test expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/skipped-test --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/skipped-test       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/skipped-test  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>   # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Write the reason, the ticket that tracks the fix and the date you will look again, on the line above: `// SKIP(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): reason`.
2. For an expired skip: fix the test and remove the skip; or, if it really must stay off, move the date and say why in the reason.
3. If the test is not needed, delete it.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
it.skip("totals the items", () => {
  expect(total([1, 2])).toBe(3);
});
```

#### Do

```js
// SKIP(SHOP-77, 2027-01-31): flaky on the CI clock
it.skip("totals the items", () => {
  expect(total([1, 2])).toBe(3);
});
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
xtest("renders the badge", () => {
  render(<Badge />);
});
```

#### Do

```jsx
// SKIP(UI-8, 2027-02-15): waits for the new icon font
xtest("renders the badge", () => {
  render(<Badge />);
});
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
describe.skip("cart", () => {
  it("totals the items", () => expect(total([1, 2])).toBe(3));
});
```

#### Do

```ts
// SKIP(SHOP-90, 2027-03-01): rewritten in the checkout rework
describe.skip("cart", () => {
  it("totals the items", () => expect(total([1, 2])).toBe(3));
});
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
test.skip("renders the badge", () => {
  render(<Badge />);
});
```

#### Do

```tsx
// SKIP(UI-8, 2027-02-15): waits for the new icon font
test.skip("renders the badge", () => {
  render(<Badge />);
});
```
